title: SlimPipe: Memory-Thrifty and Efficient Pipeline Parallelism for Long-Context LLM Training
problem: Pipeline parallelism for long-context LLMs faces severe activation memory pressure from multi-microbatch accumulation and pipeline bubbles limiting MFU efficiency
motivation: Long-context LLM training requires extreme parallelism; reducing memory overhead while minimizing bubbles is critical for efficient training on limited GPU memory
method: The method breaks the long input sequence into equal-sized chunks and feeds them through multiple GPU devices in parallel using a pipeline (new data starts processing while previous data is still computing). It uses a 1F1B schedule—each device performs one forward pass and one backward pass in sequence—to keep the pipeline full and reduce idle waiting time. Since causal attention (where each token can only reference previous tokens, not future ones) creates unequal work across devices, the system redistributes computation to balance the load and prevent bottlenecks.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining uniform sequence slicing with intelligent workload redistribution to enable pipeline parallelism on extreme-length contexts up to 2 million tokens.
contributions: Uniform sequence slicing constraining activation memory to single microbatch
Workload redistribution balancing causal attention imbalance
Near-zero memory overhead for activation management
1.57x MFU improvement vs SOTA at 512K context; 45% MFU sustained on 256 GPUs for 2M context
limitations: Limited to uniformly distributed sequence slicing; workload redistribution cost not quantified; GPU synchronization overhead not discussed
